comments.body:
## Additional in-scope case found while fixing `326f-595a-088b-40a5`

A second place where `fsck --output json` disagrees with — or discards — what the text surface
reports:

**An UNINITIALISED store renders as CLEAN in JSON.** `src/rebar/_commands/fsck.py:246-268`
(`_missing_tracker_result`) returns exit `1` and, in JSON mode (`:260-262`), writes

```
{"issues": [], "fixed": [], "issue_count": 0}
```

with **empty stderr** — byte-indistinguishable from a healthy store apart from the exit code.
The actual diagnostic ("Error: ticket system not initialized (<tracker> not found). Run 'ticket
init' first.", plus the tracker.dir mismatch hint) is written **only on the TEXT path**
(`:263-267`). A JSON consumer therefore cannot tell "there is no store here" from "the store is
fine", and the mismatch hint — the one line that tells an operator they moved `tracker.dir`
without migrating — is lost entirely.

Note this also makes `returncode == 1 with an empty issues[]` the in-band signature of a run
that never happened. Bug 326f relies on exactly that (the exit code is derived from `_scan`'s
COUNTED tally while `issues[]` is the superset of every emitted `KIND:` line, so a real scan
exiting 1 always has a non-empty `issues[]`) to raise instead of returning a fabricated clean
report from `rebar.fsck_report()`. If this ticket changes the uninitialised-store JSON payload,
**check `fsck_report` in `src/rebar/_lib_reads.py`** — it should keep failing closed, ideally on
a more explicit signal than the empty-issues coincidence.

Suggested addition to this ticket's scope: the JSON payload for an unscannable store should
carry the diagnostic (e.g. an `issues[]` entry of a `not_initialized` kind, or the existing
`compat_error`-style side channel that `_transform_json` already supports for incompatible
stores), so text and JSON agree.

## Summary

`rebar fsck` has TWO different issue counts and they disagree.

- **The exit code** comes from `_scan`'s counter, which respects each finding's `is_issue` flag:
  `src/rebar/_commands/fsck.py:242-243` (`rc = 0 if issue_count == 0 else 1`), fed by
  `src/rebar/_commands/fsck_tracker_health.py:58-70`.
- **`--output json`'s `issue_count`** is recomputed independently as `len(issues)` at
  `src/rebar/_commands/fsck.py:139`, where `issues` is EVERY uppercase `KIND:` line the text
  report emitted (`fsck.py:120-138`) — with no knowledge of `is_issue`.

So the never-counted kinds inflate the JSON count while contributing nothing to the exit code.

## Affected kinds (all pre-existing)

- `PUSH_PENDING` — `fsck_tracker_health.py:232-238` (`is_issue=False`)
- `TRACKER_DIRTY_TMP_EVENT` — `fsck_tracker_health.py:276-281` (`is_issue=False`)
- `WARN:` lines — index-lock (`fsck_scan.py:157-161`), forward-compat (`fsck_scan.py:244-249`)
- `STATUS_FORK_RESOLVED` — joins this set as of bug `326f-595a-088b-40a5`

The divergence is already observable and test-pinned today:
`tests/unit/test_doctor_dirty_tree.py:202-218` asserts `rc == 1` while
`tracker_dirty_tmp_event` sits inside `payload["issues"]`, and
`tests/unit/test_unsigned_env_fsck_heldout.py:118-128` documents that JSON
`issue_count == len(issues)` literally.

## Why it matters

A JSON consumer that gates on `issue_count > 0` reaches a different verdict than a shell
consumer that gates on the exit code, against the same store and the same run. `docs/user-guide.md:449-450`
tells users `TRACKER_DIRTY_TMP_EVENT` is "never counted" — which is true of the exit code and
false of the JSON payload they were pointed at.

## Discovered from

Bug `326f-595a-088b-40a5` (cutprice-untameable-stork), while making the MCP fsck tool return a
structured result. Deliberately NOT fixed there: reconciling the two counts changes CLI JSON
output for kinds that bug does not own, so it needs its own decision (does `issue_count` mean
"lines emitted" or "things that failed the run"? — likely: keep `issues[]` complete, make
`issue_count` the counted subset, and consider an explicit per-issue `counted` boolean).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Decide the meaning of `--output json`'s `issue_count` and make it agree with the exit code.
- [ ] `issues[]` keeps carrying every emitted finding, counted or not (no loss of information).
- [ ] Every never-counted kind above behaves per the decision, with a test pinning each.
- [ ] `docs/user-guide.md`'s "never counted" wording is true of both surfaces.
compiled_state.title: fsck --output json issue_count disagrees with the exit code for never-counted finding kinds
